incident-bot: :rotating_light: HIGH: GPU_POOL_THROTTLE for cluster=eu-central-1 — inference queue buildup > 10k, HPA reading stalled. Paging oncall.
Priya Kapoor: I'm oncall. Seeing paged alerts from SRE and multiple customer errors. Marco, can you check HPA and prometheus-adapter status?
Marco Ruiz: looking. `kubectl -n inference get hpa` shows Desired: 0 -> Current: 12 but `events` include "Failed to get custom metrics: timeout".
Samir Das: prometheus-adapter pod is up but responding very slowly. `kubectl -n monitoring logs deploy/prometheus-adapter --tail=100`:

```
E0629 15:04:12.123 adapter.go:82] error fetching: context deadline exceeded
```

Samir Das: metrics-server also reporting stale node metrics; `kubectl top nodes` times out intermittently.
Priya Kapoor: Autoscaler: cluster-autoscaler logs show `scale_up blocked by resource quota or limits`. infra-bot, can you confirm quotas for GPUs in eu-central-1?
infra-bot: Querying cloud: GPU quota remaining in eu-central-1 = 0/100 (quota exhausted). Opened ticket CLD-1087.
Nina Gomez: Customer impact: some low-volume customers see 429s, several large tenants on burst capacity experiencing increased queue times causing timeouts.
Marco Ruiz: Quick mitigation plan: 1) try CPU-HPA fallback for non-critical pools 2) free GPUs by draining cache/preemptible jobs 3) reduce prometheus retention to lower memory on prometheus to stabilize adapter
Priya Kapoor: Can we flip HPA to use `metrics.k8s.io` CPU proxy when custom metrics fail? We have a runbook script for fallback.
Samir Das: Running fallback script now: `kubectl -n inference apply -f runbooks/hpa-cpu-fallback.yaml` — it patches HPAs to use cpu metric when `custom.metrics` discovery fails.

deploy-bot: applied patch hpa/fallback-inference

Samir Das: Fallback engaged for `inference-worker-*` HPAs. They will scale based on CPU for next 30m.
Marco Ruiz: CPU-based scaling triggered, but it is slow for GPU-bound workloads. It helps some dispatcher pods.
Priya Kapoor: We need immediate capacity. Marco, can you evict low-priority GPU jobs?
Marco Ruiz: Starting selective drain on nodes with label `gpu=true && priority=low`

```
kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide --selector=priority=low -o name | xargs -r kubectl -n inference delete pod
```

Marco Ruiz: Evicted ~18 pods, freed 6 GPUs. Queue dropped slightly.
Nina Gomez: Customer comms: Posting to status: "Investigating degraded performance caused by GPU capacity exhaustion; engineering mitigation in progress."
Priya Kapoor: Good. Also attempt to restart prometheus-adapter to clear stuck connections.
Samir Das: Restarting adapter `kubectl -n monitoring rollout restart deployment/prometheus-adapter`.
Samir Das: Adapter came up but still seeing high latency to Prometheus. Prometheus server logs:

```
level=warn ts="2024-06-29T15:07:01Z" msg="TSDB head block opening: high series churn"
level=error ts="2024-06-29T15:07:05Z" msg="querier.query returned error: context deadline exceeded"
```

Samir Das: Looks like a retention spike from a malformed scrape or a runaway label cardinality increase. I've temporarily reduced retention and compaction settings to relieve memory.
Marco Ruiz: Patch applied: `kubectl -n monitoring patch configmap prometheus-config --patch '{"data":{"storage.tsdb.retention.size":"2GB"}}'` then restarted pods.

deploy-bot: configmap/prometheus-config patched

infra-bot: Note: changing retention will cause loss of oldest metrics. Quota ticket still open.
Priya Kapoor: After adapter restart + retention change, adapter now returns custom metrics and HPA sees queue_length again.
Marco Ruiz: HPA made scale decision but cluster-autoscaler still blocked by quota. We can only scale within existing nodes. Suggest we spin ephemeral preemptible GPU VMs via infra playbook.
infra-bot: Preemptible GPUs available: 10 nodes. Spinning up 4 now via automation.
infra-bot: Requested ephemeral nodes created: gpu-preempt-1..4 added to ASG.
Marco Ruiz: New nodes joined the cluster, kubelet registered, pods scheduling. GPU capacity increased by 8 GPUs. Queue dropping fast.
Nina Gomez: Excellent. Errors dropping to baseline for most customers. Two dedicated-pool tenants remain impacted (pinned). Recommending manual migration or permission to temporarily overprovision their pool.
Priya Kapoor: Marco, can you apply temporary override to dedicated pools to allow preemptible nodes to accept their pods?
Marco Ruiz: Adding toleration/taint changes to allow placement on preemptibles for the next 1h.

```
kubectl -n inference patch deployment dedicated-pool-acme --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"tolerations":[{"key":"preemptible","operator":"Exists","effect":"NoSchedule"}]}}}}'
```

deploy-bot: deployment/dedicated-pool-acme patched

Marco Ruiz: Acme and Gamma deployments now scheduling onto preemptible nodes. Their latency improving.
Priya Kapoor: Summary of immediate mitigations: 1) HPA CPU fallback engaged 2) Evicted low-priority pods freeing GPUs 3) Reduced prometheus retention and restarted adapter 4) Provisioned ephemeral preemptible GPU nodes 5) Relaxed scheduling for dedicated tenants
Nina Gomez: Customer message updated: "Mitigation measures applied; performance improving. We may use short-lived extra capacity. No data loss. Further updates in 10 minutes."
Samir Das: Follow-ups to create: - harden prometheus against cardinality spikes - add adapter discovery/latency alerts - automate HPA fallback when custom metrics unavailable - clear escalation path for GPU quotas and preemptible usage - review dedicated pool overflow policy
Priya Kapoor: I'll assign follow-ups in the incident board. Handing off monitoring to Marco for the next 90m.
Marco Ruiz: Taking over. I'll keep this channel updated and escalate if queue grows again.
incident-bot: Incident state UPDATED -> MONITORING at 1719961199. Follow-up tickets created: INF-564, METRICS-412, QUOTA-1087
